# Growthbook <> Sunfire - Intro
Date: 2026-10-08 | Duration: 38.470001220703125m

## Summary
The team aims to launch foundational experimentation and feature flagging by Q4 using GrowthBook rather than building internally. The platform offers Bayesian analysis, guardrail metrics, sequential testing, multi-armed and contextual bandits, sticky bucketing, and backend and frontend SDKs. Its warehouse-native design connects directly to Postgres, supports historical experiment imports, and enables SQL, CSV, or API-based reporting. Self-hosting is preferred because the team handles PHI, expects traffic growth, and needs secure connectivity to Postgres behind a VPN; cloud hosting offers automatic updates but includes CDN costs and connectivity considerations. GrowthBook supports open-source deployment, SOC 2, HIPAA, BAAs, and disabling AI features when required. A roughly two-week trial may include historical data onboarding, dashboards, and direct technical support, followed by a POC scoping call and confirmation of legal requirements. Seat-based pricing for self-hosted usage was viewed as more predictable for backend-heavy applications.

## Keywords
warehouse-native, feature flagging, experimentation, multi-armed bandits, healthcare compliance, self-hosted trial

## Action Items

Attend the Proof of Concept (POC) scoping call scheduled for the Wednesday following the current week to clarify success criteria and address legal or technical questions (35:14)

**Dan Wathne**
Send a follow-up email to Sunfire with the booking link for the POC scoping call (35:32)
Provide the license key for the self-hosted trial to Sunfire via secure note sharing (35:06)

# Growthbook <> Sunfire - POC Scoping
Date: 2026-10-14 | Duration: 45.709999084472656m

## Summary
The team established a separate production environment from the parent company and plans to manage infrastructure primarily with Terraform and Argo while limiting services outside AWS. The GrowthBook trial will be self-hosted, using Postgres, the Java SDK, enterprise functions, and server-sent events with a proxy or edge worker. Synthetic call data will be loaded into a new Postgres instance, while a standalone Mongo database will be used during the trial as the team evaluates Amazon DocumentDB compatibility. Multi-tenant analysis will use separate GrowthBook projects per tenant, with tags, scope filters, runtime attributes, and demographic data supporting cross-tenant analysis. GrowthBook’s automatic schema inference, point-and-click metric creation, targeting, cohorting, and guardrail metrics were demonstrated. Onboarding is expected by Monday at the latest, with license access, a private Slack channel, weekly check-ins, and an initial estimate of five users. Pricing and seat discussions will follow, and enterprise support will provide direct engineer access.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, feature flagging, self-hosted, PostgreSQL, multi-tenant, synthetic data
